transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope it's okay that I came in. I just... well, I've been feeling a little stressed at work lately. I drive for a transit company, and I'm probably just overthinking things, but... I'm here because I've noticed that dispatch and compliance seem to be tracking my route changes through the computer system. And, um, there are these little comments on the radio. People tell me it's just normal oversight, and I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining or being difficult, but I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. Does that make sense? I just want to do a good job, you know?
Do you think these people are reporting on you because they have something against you personally?

Um... well, I really don't want to think anyone hates me. I try so hard to get along with everyone, I really do. But... like I was just saying with dispatch tracking my routes on the computer... it just feels really specific to me. 

I know my supervisor says it's just normal oversight, and I'm sure they're mostly just doing their jobs, right? But then I hear those little comments on the radio, and... I don't know, I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me, maybe to get me in trouble? I hope I don't sound paranoid or difficult saying that. I just want to be a good employee and do things right. Is it okay that I'm worried about this?
Do you think there's any possibility that you're misinterpreting the comments on the radio or the tracking of your routes?

I mean... yes, absolutely. I try to tell myself that all the time. I really, really don't want to be the kind of person who makes a big deal out of nothing, and I know you're just asking to help me. I appreciate that. 

But... um... it's just so hard to ignore. I try to believe people when they say it's just normal oversight, I really do. But I can still see how dispatch and compliance are tracking my exact route changes through the computer system. And those little comments on the radio... I really wish I was just misunderstanding them, but I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm probably sounding so stubborn right now by repeating that. I don't mean to be difficult, I promise. Does that make sense why I'd still be worried, even if I'm trying not to be?
Do you think anyone is out to get you or harm you in any way?

Oh, no, no! I really don't think anyone wants to physically hurt me. I know saying something like that would sound really... well, I don't want you to think I'm totally crazy or anything. I'm so sorry if I gave that impression! 

It's not about physical harm. It's just... well, kind of like what I was saying before. I know I keep bringing it up, and I really don't mean to sound like a broken record, but it's just the way dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes on the computer. And those little comments on the radio. It feels more like they want to ruin my job, you know? Like, even when people keep telling me it's just normal oversight, I can just tell those certain drivers are reporting on me to get me fired or in trouble. Not to hurt me, just... push me out of the company. 

Does that answer your question okay? I really hope I'm making sense and not just wasting your time.
Do you think your belief that certain drivers are reporting on you could be wrong?

I... well, I want to say yes. I really want to be able to say that I'm just wrong about all of it. I know that's what I'm supposed to think, and I'm trying so hard to be reasonable about this. I don't want to be a problem for anyone.

But... every time I go to work, it's the exact same thing. I log in, and I can see how dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system. And then I hear the little comments on the radio... and it just feels so real. Like, even when my supervisor or anyone else tells me it's just normal oversight, I just... I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear, and I'm probably being so frustrating right now. I really am trying to look at it from other perspectives. It's just so hard when it feels so obvious to me. Am I being too difficult by saying that? I really don't mean to be.
How long have you been feeling like certain drivers are reporting on you?

Um... let's see. I really hope I haven't let this drag on too long without saying anything. I didn't want to make a fuss or seem like a complainer, you know? But... I guess it's been... well, the tracking through the computer system and those radio comments, they've felt really clear to me for about the past two months. 

I know two months probably sounds like a long time to let something like this bother me, and I'm so sorry I didn't just handle it better on my own. I just kept hoping it would stop so I wouldn't have to bother you or anyone else with it. Does that timeline help you at all? I really hope I'm giving you the right information.
Do you think it's possible for you to change your mind about certain drivers reporting on you?

I... I really want to tell you yes. I'd love to just agree and say I can change my mind, because I don't want to be stubborn or make your job harder. I know I'm probably sounding so unreasonable right now, and I'm really sorry about that. 

It's just... well, I know I keep bringing up the same things, but when I see dispatch and compliance tracking my route changes through the computer system, and then I hear those little comments on the radio... it's just impossible for me to ignore. Even when people tell me it's just normal oversight, and I try so, so hard to believe them, I can just tell certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I really wish I could just turn it off and think differently, I really do. I'd love to just drop it so I wouldn't be such a bother. Am I being too frustrating? I really hope you're not upset with me for being so stuck on this.
Can you think of any other reason why dispatch and compliance might be tracking your route changes through the computer system?

I mean... yes, I try to tell myself that all the time. I really do. I know that in most jobs, dispatch tracks things just to make sure deliveries are on time, or for safety, or... or just normal oversight, like everyone keeps telling me. And I really want to believe that. I want to be the kind of employee who just accepts that and doesn't make a big deal out of things. 

But... it's just so hard when I hear those little comments on the radio. It makes the computer tracking feel like it's... more than just oversight. It feels like they're coordinating with the other drivers to report on me. I know I keep saying that, and I'm so sorry if I sound like a broken record. I really am trying to see it the way you're suggesting. I just... I can't shake the feeling that I'm right about the drivers reporting on me. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not sounding too crazy by saying that.
Have you ever considered that your interpretation of the comments on the radio might be incorrect?

I... well, yes, I have. I really try to be open-minded, and I know you're just trying to help me see all the angles. I don't want to seem like I'm just dismissing what you're saying, because I value your opinion so much. 

I've told myself a hundred times that maybe I'm just mishearing the radio, or that the little comments are just... you know, regular chatter. I really want it to be that simple. I want to be wrong, honestly. It would be so much easier if I was just misinterpreting things. 

But... when I put it all together—the dispatch and compliance tracking my route changes in the system, and then those specific comments on the radio... it just lines up too perfectly. Even when people keep telling me it's normal oversight, I just... I can tell those certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm so sorry, I know I'm probably being really difficult right now. I hope you know I'm really trying my best to think about this the way you're asking me to. Am I doing okay? I just don't want to disappoint you by being so stuck on this.
Do you think it's possible that your belief about the drivers reporting on you could change if you found out more information about the tracking and comments?

I... I really want to say yes. I'd love to tell you that if someone just sat down and showed me the computer logs, or explained exactly what the radio chatter meant, that I'd completely change my mind. I know that's what a reasonable person would do, and I'm trying so hard to be reasonable for you. I don't want you to think I'm completely closed off to logic.

But... it's just so difficult. Even when people try to explain it away and tell me it's just normal oversight... the way dispatch and compliance track my route changes, and those specific little comments on the radio... it all just feels so real to me. Deep down, I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I know I'm probably disappointing you by saying that, and I'm really, really sorry. I wish I could just snap out of it and say, "Oh, you're right, I was totally wrong!" It would make things so much easier for everyone. I'm trying my best to be open, I promise. Is it okay that I still feel this way? I really hope I'm not making you too frustrated with me.
Would you change your mind about the drivers reporting on you if your supervisor showed you proof that the tracking and comments were for a different purpose?

I... I know I should say yes to that. I really do. If my supervisor sat me down and showed me proof... I know the right thing to do would be to just accept it and move on. I want to be the kind of person who can just look at a piece of paper and say, "Okay, I was wrong, thank you for showing me." I really don't want to be a problem for my supervisor, or for you. 

But... even if they showed me something that looked like proof... I think I would still struggle. Because the things I'm experiencing... the way dispatch and compliance track my route changes in the computer system, and those little comments on the radio... it's not just a misunderstanding on my part. Even when they try to tell me it's just normal oversight, I can still tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm so sorry. I know that sounds terrible, like I'm just being stubborn and refusing to listen to reason. I promise I'm not trying to be difficult. I just... I can't ignore what I know is happening, even if I really, really want to for everyone else's sake. Does that make me a bad patient? I'm trying so hard to be honest with you, but I hate feeling like I'm letting you down by not being able to just let this go.
Can you think of any reason why you might be interpreting the comments on the radio and the tracking of your route changes incorrectly?

I... I try to think of reasons all the time. I know you want me to find a logical explanation, and I really, really try to do that for you. I tell myself, maybe I'm just stressed from work, or maybe I'm just being too sensitive about my job performance. I know everyone keeps telling me it’s just normal oversight, and I want to believe them. I really do. 

But... when I look at how dispatch and compliance are actually logging those route changes in the computer system... and then I hear those little comments on the radio... it just... it doesn't feel like a mistake. Even when I try to brush it off and tell myself I'm just overthinking, I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm sorry, I know I just keep repeating the same thing to you. I really am trying to look at it your way and find a reason why I'm wrong, I promise. Am I... am I doing this wrong? I don't want you to think I'm not trying my hardest to figure this out with you.
Would seeing proof from your supervisor that the tracking and comments are for a legitimate work purpose change your belief that certain drivers are reporting on you?

I... oh, I feel terrible, because I know you just asked me about my supervisor, and I must not be giving you the answer you need. I'm so sorry. I really don't want to frustrate you. 

I really, really wish that seeing a document or getting proof from them would just make it all go away. That would be wonderful, and I'd love to just agree with you and say yes. But... it's just that when I actually look at how dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system... and then I hear those specific little comments on the radio... it's just so ingrained in me. People keep telling me it’s just normal oversight, and I always nod and smile because I don't want to cause a fuss at work, but... I can just tell that certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I feel awful that I can't just say yes and make this easy for you. I really hope you don't think I'm just being difficult on purpose. I'm trying so hard to be cooperative. Are you... are you mad at me for not being able to change my mind? I really want to be a good patient, I just don't know how to turn off what I know is happening.
How much time do you spend thinking about the possibility of certain drivers reporting on you during a typical day?

I... oh, I'm not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I don't want you to think I just sit around all day obsessing over it, because I don't! I really try to focus on my job and be a good employee. I don't spend... I don't think I spend an unusual amount of time on it. 

I mean, it crosses my mind, of course, especially when I'm driving and I hear the radio, but I try really hard to just push it away and do my work. I don't want it to seem like it's taking over my life or anything. Is... is it normal to think about things from work a little bit during the day? I hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm too distracted. I really do try to just do my job the best I can.
Do you think there's anything that could happen or anything someone could tell you that would make you completely change your mind about the drivers reporting on you?

I... I really wish I could say yes. I know that's the answer you're hoping for, and I want so badly to be able to just... just let it all go and tell you that someone could talk me out of it. I really do. 

But... I mean, when I'm sitting there and I see the way dispatch and compliance are logging every single one of my route changes in the computer... and then I hear those little comments on the radio... it's just... I can just tell certain drivers are reporting on me. Even when my supervisor or anyone else tells me it's just normal oversight, and I smile and say okay because I don't want to be difficult... inside, I just know what's happening. 

I'm so sorry. I feel like I'm failing this test or something. I'm trying so hard to be open-minded for you, I promise I am. Does... does it make me a bad patient if I can't just change my mind? I really am trying my best to work with you on this.
Do you think your belief that certain drivers are reporting on you is based on facts or just a feeling you have?

I... well, I really want to say it's just a feeling, because I know that sounds so much better, and I really don't want to sound unreasonable to you. I know how it must seem. But... I mean, it's based on things that are actually happening, you know? 

Like I was saying, it's the actual tracking in the computer system by dispatch and compliance, and... and the specific comments on the radio. Those are real things that happen during my shift. So... I guess it feels like it's based on facts to me, even though I know other people say it's just normal oversight. I really wish I could just brush it off as a feeling and tell you what you want to hear. I'm sorry, I hope that doesn't make me sound too stubborn or... or crazy. I'm just trying to be honest with you about what I'm seeing. Is that... is it okay that I answered it that way?
Do you think your belief that certain drivers are reporting on you is something that might not be true, even if it feels real to you?

I... I try to tell myself that. I really do. I'll sit there and say, 'Maybe it's just in my head, maybe everyone is right and it's just normal oversight.' I want to believe that, I promise I do, because I know it would make things so much easier for you and for my job, and I really don't want to be difficult. 

But... like I mentioned before, the reason I'm even here is because of how dispatch and compliance have been tracking my route changes through the computer system. And then the little comments on the radio happen... and I just, I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. I can't just pretend it's not happening when I see it, even though I really, really wish I could just agree with you and make this easier. 

I'm sorry, I know that's probably the wrong answer. Does it... does it make sense why it's so hard for me to just say it isn't true? I hope you aren't frustrated with me.
Would you still believe certain drivers are reporting on you if you were shown evidence that proved no one was?

I... I know you want me to say yes. And I really, really want to be the kind of patient who can just look at evidence and say, 'Oh, okay, I was wrong.' I want to be easy to work with, I promise. 

But... if someone showed me a piece of paper or a report that said no one was doing it... I think I would just wonder if the report was fake, or if they were just hiding it better. Because... well, like I said, I'm here because of the tracking. The way dispatch and compliance monitor my route changes in the computer system, and... and those comments on the radio. It's just so clear to me. Even when my supervisor tries to show me that it's just normal oversight, and I nod and try to agree so I don't upset them... I still know those drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm so sorry. I know I'm probably being really difficult right now, and I hate that. I just... I can't ignore what I'm seeing every day. Does that... does that make me sound completely unreasonable? I'm trying so hard to do this right for you.
Do you think anything could ever convince you that the drivers are not reporting on you?

I... I really want to say yes. I want to tell you that there's something that could just make it all go away, because I know that's what I'm supposed to say. I want to be able to just... accept it and move on, so I'm not taking up so much of your time with this. 

But... I just don't know how I could ever un-see it, you know? Because I'm here... I'm sitting right here talking to you because of what dispatch and compliance are doing. They track every little route change I make in the computer system, and then I hear those little comments on the radio. And I know people keep telling me it's just normal oversight, and I always smile and say 'okay' because I don't want to cause trouble... but I can just tell. I can tell certain drivers are reporting on me. 

I'm sorry, I feel like I'm failing this interview by giving you the same answer again. I just... I don't know what could convince me otherwise when it's happening right in front of me. Is it... is it really bad that I can't think of anything that would change my mind? I'm sorry if I'm being a frustrating patient.
How much of your daily thoughts are occupied with the idea that certain drivers are reporting on you?

I... well, I really try not to let it take over my day. I promise I do my best to focus on my job and just be a good employee. I don't want you to think I'm just sitting around obsessing over it instead of working. 

But... it's hard not to think about it a lot. Because, like I've been saying, the whole reason I'm here is because dispatch and compliance are tracking my route changes through the computer system. And then I hear those little comments on the radio while I'm driving... and even though everyone tells me it's just normal oversight, and I try so hard to just agree with them so I don't seem difficult... I can still tell certain drivers are reporting on me. 

So it's just... it's on my mind a lot while I'm working. Probably more than it should be. I'm sorry, I know I shouldn't let it distract me so much. Is that... is that a really bad sign? I hope you don't think less of me for letting it take up so much of my thoughts.
